name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.dualKer
source: ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ_[l] M] (M' : Type) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module ℤ_[l] M'] (T : M →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] M'),
LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) T) = LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (LinearMap.ker T).subtype) ∧
∀ p : Submodule ℤ_[l] M, Function.Surjective (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) p.subtype) := by
have hle : LinearMap.ker T ≤ LinearMap.ker f := by
let g0 : LinearMap.range T →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l :=
obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hI.out (LinearMap.range T).subtype Subtype.val_injective g0
have := hh ⟨T x, LinearMap.mem_range_self T x⟩
· obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hI.out p.subtype Subtype.val_injective g
show: For an ℓ-adic linear map T from M to M′, the characters on M obtained by precomposition with T are exactly the characters trivial on its kernel. Restriction to every submodule of M is surjective on characters.
strategy: A character vanishing on the kernel factors through the image of T. Injectivity of QZ extends the resulting character to M′ and also extends any character of a submodule to M.

steps.claim: Fix an ℤℓ-linear map T from M to M′ and write D(A) = Homℤℓ(A,ℚℓ/ℤℓ). The target ℚℓ/ℤℓ is injective as an ℤℓ-module, so maps into it extend across submodule inclusions.
steps.snippet:
∀ p : Submodule ℤ_[l] M, Function.Surjective (LinearMap.lcomp ℤ_[l] (QZ l) p.subtype) := by
  intro l _ M _ _ M' _ _ T
  have hI := PropA.qzInj l

steps.claim: The image of T* is the kernel of restriction D(M) → D(ker T). Moreover, for every P ⊆ M, each character on P has an extension to M, hence D(M) → D(P) is surjective.

children.claim: A character f on M vanishes on ker T exactly when f = h ∘ T for some h on M′. In the reverse direction f descends to im T and the descended character extends to M′.
For f ∈ D(M), membership in im(T*) means f = h ∘ T for some h ∈ D(M′). Membership in the restriction kernel means f(x) = 0 for every x ∈ ker T.
A pullback vanishes wherever T vanishes. Conversely, vanishing on ker T gives a character on M/ker T ≅ im T, which injectivity of the target extends to M′.
If f = h ∘ T and x ∈ ker T, then f(x) = h(Tx) = h(0) = 0. Thus f has zero restriction to ker T.
children.snippet:
· rintro ⟨g, rfl⟩
      ext ⟨x, hx⟩
      simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, Submodule.subtype_apply,
        LinearMap.zero_apply]
      rw [LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx, map_zero]

children.claim: If f vanishes on ker T, define g₀ on im T by g₀(Tx) = f(x). Extending g₀ to a character h on M′ gives h(Tx) = f(x) for every x ∈ M, so f is a pullback.
For x ∈ ker T, evaluating the zero restriction at x gives f(x) = 0. Thus ker T ⊆ ker f.
children.snippet:
have hle : LinearMap.ker T ≤ LinearMap.ker f := by
        intro x hx
        have := LinearMap.congr_fun hf ⟨x, hx⟩
        simpa using this

children.claim: Factor f through M/ker T and the inverse of M/ker T ≅ im T to obtain g₀ on im T. Injectivity of ℚℓ/ℤℓ extends it to h on M′, with h(Tx) = g₀(Tx) since Tx ∈ im T.
children.snippet:
let g0 : LinearMap.range T →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l :=
        ((LinearMap.ker T).liftQ f hle).comp (LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange T).symm.toLinearMap
      obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hI.out (LinearMap.range T).subtype Subtype.val_injective g0
      refine ⟨h, ?_⟩
      ext x
      simp only [LinearMap.lcomp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
      have := hh ⟨T x, LinearMap.mem_range_self T x⟩
      simp only [Submodule.subtype_apply] at this

children.claim: Under im T ≅ M/ker T, the element Tx corresponds to x+ker T. The quotient character takes this class to f(x), so h(Tx) = g₀(Tx) = f(x).
For P ⊆ M and g ∈ D(P), injectivity gives h ∈ D(M) with h(x) = g(x) for each x ∈ P. The restriction of h therefore equals g and restriction is surjective.
children.snippet:
· obtain ⟨h, hh⟩ := hI.out p.subtype Subtype.val_injective g
    refine ⟨h, ?_⟩
    ext x
    simpa using hh x

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
